newsitem.title: FRANCE: French strike may cost agro-food firms dearly.
newsitem.headline: French strike may cost agro-food firms dearly.

text.p: French agro-food firms could incur heavy financial losses if a nationwide truckers' strike now in its ninth day goes on much longer, industry officials said on Tuesday.

Because the strike is disrupting the transport of food and raw farm materials to stores and production plants, some firms have already temporarily laid off employees while others may do so in coming days, they said.
Truckers who are demanding better pay and shorter working hours have set up blockades of roads and fuel depots across the nation, limiting traffic and supplies to gas stations.
"If the situation were to last two or three more days, we could all be on temporary leave," said Philippe Cousseau, head of logistics for the National Agro-Food Industry Association ANIA.
He warned the crisis could cripple the agro-food industry and result in "very heavy" financial losses.
In 1995 agro-food sector employed 397,000 people and generated sales of 735 billion francs.
Fresh dairy products, poultry, ready-made meals, fruits and vegetables were among the hardest by the crisis.
Animal feed producers, which are working with tight stocks, warned that not enough soy, sunflower and rapemeal was reaching their plants.

Some 20 animal feed plants had already temporary laid off employees and about 100 plants of the nation's 380 might be affected by Wednesday, said Paul Hervieu, communication director of the National Animal Feed Makers Association (SNIA).
SNIA said if the strike continued pigs and poultry would at risk as they could not be adequately fed.
